ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
【Story 1】The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports. One day, there is a table-tennis table in the garage as a surprise from his parents. The boy challenges his dad to a match.

The boy faces a big choice: challenge himself with endurance and courage, or avoid difficulties.

[Path of Avoidance] He misses the ball, bruises his elbow, and gives up. He refuses to play the next week and turns down his mom's suggestion to play his brother. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are obstacles—best avoided.

[Path of Embracing Challenge] He picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still wins easily, but the boy is learning. He challenges his brother too. He practices until he joins the regional team—reaching the national finals. He sneaks the ball past his opponent at match point. He has become truly awesome!

This is the story of Matthew Syed, a former British national table-tennis team member. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried new things, discovered his passion, and became tough facing difficult tasks. You, too, can find your own "table tennis." Embrace the challenge and never give up.

【Story 2】Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Being a real teenager presents its own challenges. Resilience is the ability to adapt to challenging experiences. Humans can recover from hardship—and you can develop this skill. Resilience will not prevent problems, but helps you face them.

Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. Resilience means: you experience, feel, fail, hurt, and fall—but you keep going. It takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 학교 탁구부에 가입한 후 연습을 더 하고 싶었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 소년은 학교 탁구부에 최근 가입했으며 연습을 더 하고 싶었다: 원문 일치
❌ ① 소년이 직접 탁구대를 구입했다: 부모의 깜짝 선물
❌ ③ 부모가 소년에게 탁구대를 보여주기 전에 알려줬다: surprise
❌ ④ 소년은 탁구를 처음 접했다: recently joined the club
det.tip: 원문: He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.

ch: 소년이 직접 탁구대를 구입하여 차고에 설치했다.
소년은 학교 탁구부에 최근 가입했으며 연습을 더 하고 싶었다.
부모는 소년에게 미리 탁구대가 있다고 알려주었다.

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem: 회피형 소년에 대한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 소년은 형과의 대결을 거절했다(turns down). '수락했다'는 원문과 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 소년은 형과의 대결을 흔쾌히 수락했다: 원문은 turns down → 불일치
❌ ① 팔꿈치에 여전히 통증이 있었다: 원문 일치
❌ ② 도전을 장애물로 여겼다: 원문 일치
❌ ④ 피하는 것이 최선이라고 믿었다: 원문 일치
det.tip: turns down = 거절하다. 소년은 형과의 대결 제안을 거절했다.

ch: 소년은 도전을 피하는 것이 최선이라고 믿었다.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion.
questions.stem:
다음 문장이 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Matthew Syed의 이야기는 허구적인 이야기처럼 보이지만, 영국 국가대표 탁구팀 출신의 실화이다."

det.korean: 원문: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed.
det.analysis: 허구처럼 보이지만 실화 → T(일치)
det.tip: fictional tale이라고 생각할 수 있지만 However로 전환하여 true story임을 밝힘.

questions.passage: The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.
questions.stem:
다음 문장이 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"회복탄력성이 있으면 스트레스나 불안을 전혀 느끼지 않게 된다."

det.korean: 원문: having resilience does NOT mean you will never feel stressed or anxious → 여전히 느낄 수 있다.
det.analysis: 회복탄력성이 있어도 스트레스/불안 느낄 수 있음 → F(불일치)
det.tip: 이중 부정 주의: does not mean ~ never = 여전히 느낄 수 있다.

questions.passage: An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.
questions.stem:
다음 문장이 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"도전형 소년은 한 시간 후에도 아버지를 이기지 못했지만, 경험에서 배우고 있었다."

det.korean: 원문: his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience.
det.analysis: 아버지가 여전히 쉽게 이기지만 소년은 배우고 있다 → T(일치)
det.tip: but 이후가 핵심: 지고 있지만 learning from the experience

questions.passage: The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path. In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than __________, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 도전을 장애물(obstacles)로만 보는 회피형 사고.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles: 원문 일치, 피해야 할 것으로 인식
❌ ② opportunities: 기회 → 성장형에 해당
❌ ③ inspirations: 영감 → 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ advantages: 이점 → 피할 이유 없음
det.tip: 회피형: challenges = obstacles(장애물) → best avoided

questions.passage: Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own 'table tennis.' It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you __________ and never give up on what you want to achieve.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 도전을 받아들이고(embrace the challenge) 포기하지 않는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ embrace the challenge: 원문 일치
❌ ① avoid the difficulty: 회피 → 성장 마인드셋과 반대
❌ ② follow the crowd: 남을 따라가다 → 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ ignore the problem: 무시 → 문맥과 반대
det.tip: embrace the challenge = 도전을 받아들이다 — 핵심 메시지

questions.passage: He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with [endurance / endure] and courage.
questions.stem: 다음 어법상 알맞은 표현을 고르시오.

det.korean: 전치사 with 뒤에는 명사가 와야 한다. endurance(명사) vs endure(동사).
det.analysis:
✅ ① endurance (명사형): 전치사 with 뒤에 명사 필요
❌ ② endure (동사원형): 전치사 뒤 동사원형 불가
❌ ③ endured (과거형): 전치사 뒤 동사 불가
❌ ④ enduring (현재분사): 문맥상 명사가 적합
det.tip: 전치사 + 명사: with endurance and courage

questions.passage: When the ball comes flying across the net [rapid / rapidly], he misses it completely.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 동사 comes flying을 수식하는 부사가 필요하다. rapidly(부사) vs rapid(형용사).
det.analysis:
✅ ① rapidly (부사): 동사 수식 → 올바름
❌ ② rapid (형용사): 동사 수식 불가
❌ ③ rapidness (명사): 문법적으로 부적절
❌ ④ more rapid (비교급 형용사): 부사 자리에 형용사 불가
det.tip: 동사 수식 → 부사(-ly) 필수: comes flying rapidly

questions.passage: When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, [hitting / to hit] and bruising his elbow.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 결과/동시상황 분사구문: 공이 돌아오면서 팔꿈치를 치고 멍들게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① hitting (분사구문): 동시동작 표현
❌ ② to hit (to부정사): 목적 표현으로 어색
❌ ③ hit (동사원형): 접속사 없이 동사 나열 불가
❌ ④ being hit (수동 분사): 공이 치는 것이므로 능동
det.tip: 분사구문: 주절과 동시 동작 → V-ing (hitting and bruising)

questions.passage: The boy just does not feel like [taking / to take] up the challenge.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 알맞은 표현을 고르시오.

det.korean: feel like + 동명사(~ing): ~하고 싶다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① taking: feel like + V-ing 구문
❌ ② to take: feel like 뒤에 to부정사 불가
❌ ③ take: 동사원형 불가
❌ ④ took: 과거형 불가
det.tip: feel like + V-ing: ~하고 싶다 (전치사 like 뒤 동명사)

questions.passage: His dad still keeps [winning / to win] easily, but the boy is learning from the experience.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: keep + V-ing: 계속 ~하다. keep은 동명사를 목적어로 취한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① winning (동명사): keep + V-ing
❌ ② to win (to부정사): keep은 to부정사 목적어 불가
❌ ③ win (동사원형): 불가
❌ ④ won (과거형): 불가
det.tip: keep + V-ing: 계속 ~하다 (동명사만 목적어로 취하는 동사)

questions.passage: He turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 표현의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: turns down = 거절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 거절하다: turn down의 정확한 의미
❌ ① 수락하다: 반의어
❌ ③ 제안하다: suggest에 해당
❌ ④ 검토하다: review에 해당
det.tip: turn down = reject = decline(거절하다) ↔ accept(수락하다)

questions.passage: He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 단어의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: sneak = 몰래/교묘하게 넘기다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 교묘하게/살짝 넘긴다: sneak의 문맥적 의미
❌ ① 세게 강타한다: smash에 해당
❌ ③ 높이 올린다: lob에 해당
❌ ④ 멀리 던진다: throw에 해당
det.tip: sneak = 살금살금/몰래 → 상대가 반응하기 전에 교묘하게 넘김

questions.passage: ① The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. ② He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. ③ Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. ④ He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 ①~④ 중, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother, who is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder."

det.korean: 형에게 도전하는 것은 실력을 키운 후(mistakes → new skills), 지역팀 합류 전 단계이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 위치: 실수에서 배운 후 → 형 도전 → 지역팀 합류 순서
❌ ① 앞: 아직 실수에서 배우는 단계 전
❌ ③ 앞: 이미 지역팀 합류 후
❌ ④ 앞: 이미 전국대회 결승
det.tip: 시간 순서: 실수 학습 → 형 도전 → 지역팀 → 전국대회

questions.passage: So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain ①<u>unchanged</u> and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to ②<u>adapt</u> to challenging experiences. The good news is that humans can ③<u>recover</u> from pressure and hardship. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or ④<u>confident</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 원문과 다르게 쓰인 것은?

det.korean: 원문: stressed or anxious(불안한). ④ confident(자신감 있는)는 원문과 다르다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ confident: 원문은 anxious → 부적절
✅ ① unchanged: 원문 일치
✅ ② adapt: 원문 일치
✅ ③ recover: 원문 일치
det.tip: anxious(불안한) ↔ confident(자신감 있는) — 문맥상 부정적 감정이 와야 함

questions.passage: Let's ①<u>rewind</u> to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still keeps winning ②<u>easily</u>, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even ③<u>disappoints</u> himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his ④<u>dad</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 원문과 다르게 쓰인 것은?

det.korean: 원문: he even surprises himself. ③ disappoints(실망시키다)는 surprises(놀라게 하다)의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ disappoints: 원문은 surprises → 부적절
✅ ① rewind: 원문 일치
✅ ② easily: 원문 일치
✅ ④ dad: 원문 일치
det.tip: surprise(놀라게 하다) ↔ disappoint(실망시키다) — decent return에 자기 자신도 놀람

questions.passage: The answer lies in resilience—the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 각각 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

[조건] 각각 한 단어

회복탄력성은 도전적인 경험에 (A)________하는 능력이며, 면역력처럼 어려움을 (B)________함으로써 개발될 수 있다.

det.korean: (A) 적응하는 능력 / (B) 어려움을 경험해야 함.
det.analysis: 원문: (A) the ability to adapt to challenging experiences / (B) you must experience difficulties
det.tip: adapt(적응하다), experience(경험하다) — 본문에서 그대로 찾을 수 있는 단어

questions.passage: Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오.

회복탄력성은 문제를 예방하지는 않겠지만, 그것들을 직면하고 극복하는 데 도움을 줄 것이다.

[조건] ① will을 사용한 미래시제 ② prevent와 overcome 포함 ③ 15단어 이내

det.korean: 원문 그대로 영작하면 된다.
det.analysis: 원문: Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.
det.tip: will not prevent ~ but will help ~ face and overcome: 대조 구조 파악

questions.wa: Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.
accept: resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.
resilience will not prevent problems but it will help you face and overcome them.
resilience won't prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.
it will not prevent problems, but resilience will help you face and overcome them.

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be __________ (expose) to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 쓰시오.

det.korean: be exposed to: 수동태. 세균에 노출되다.
det.analysis:
expose → exposed: need to be + p.p. (수동태)
you(사람)가 세균에 '노출되는' 것이므로 수동 필요
det.tip: be exposed to = ~에 노출되다 (수동태 + 전치사 to)
